searchText: Hey, I'm not kzg guru, can someone points me where in CL client the trusted setup presets `KZG_SETUP_G1` and `KZG_SETUP_LAGRANGE` will be used? maybe in the kzg library initialization? I see `KZG_SETUP_G2` used in `verify_kzg_proof` but I don't see the others two <@504202741933932544> they will all need to be supplied as inputs to the kzg library we are working on this is the latest afaik: https://github.com/dankrad/c-kzg/tree/4844_3038/src you can look in the header file to get a sense for how they will be used and there is some bespoke format for recording them in `trusted_setup.txt` so as a CL dev, there will be some nice bindings around this library you can use and you'd just pipe in the trusted setup to it Oky good Thanks - `ROOTS_OF_UNITY` - `FIAT_SHAMIR_PROTOCOL_DOMAIN` will be part of the `trusted_setup.txt` I guess.. <xrchz> the trusted_setup.txt format does not include those <xrchz> FIAT_SHAMIR_PROTOCOL_DOMAIN is fixed in the spec <xrchz> https://github.com/dankrad/c-kzg/blob/4844_3038/src/c_kzg_4844.h#L34 implementing https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/eip4844/polynomial-commitments.md#blob <xrchz> we have the roots of unity here, but i dunno where they are specified https://github.com/dankrad/c-kzg/blob/4844_3038/src/c_kzg_4844.c#L433 You use SETUP_LAGRANGE when commuting to blobs since blobs are viewed as polynomials in Lagrange form, see: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/eip4844/polynomial-commitments.md#blob_to_kzg_commitment KZG_SETUP_G1 is useful because: - this is what the trusted setup will output, you will then transform it to the Lagrange setup - In verify, instead of bls.G1 you can/should use the degree 0 element in KZG_SETUP_G1 Libraries will usually define a primitive root, usually it’s the smallest one and this is used to generate the roots of unity for size 4096. The primitive root for the field being used should be 5, I believe the specs used 7 which may need to be changed I haven't touched that root - it's the same as whatever Ben put into original c-kzg.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: You use SETUP_LAGRANGE when commuting to blobs since blobs are viewed as polynomials in Lagrange form, see: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/eip4844/polynomial-commitments.md#blob_to_kzg_commitment

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
KZG_SETUP_G1 is useful because:

- this is what the trusted setup will output, you will then transform it to the Lagrange setup 

- In verify, instead of bls.G1 you can/should use the degree 0 element in KZG_SETUP_G1

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Libraries will usually define a primitive root, usually it’s the smallest one and this is used to generate the roots of unity for size 4096. The primitive root for the field being used should be 5, I believe the specs used 7 which may need to be changed

excerpts.author: xrchz
excerpts.content: I haven't touched that root - it's the same as whatever Ben put into original c-kzg.
